acceptanceCriteria: On Mac, report directly observed verifier exit, WI-managed direct-child reaping, original-group signal facts where applicable, and unproved closure of unmanaged descendants as separate facts. A normal command may contribute to formal managed-process verification only after its registered direct child is confirmed reaped; no complete-tree claim follows.

Timeout, parent disconnect, output saturation, failed group or direct-child termination, and cleanup errors return after bounded observation. Record actual signal and kill results and whether the directly owned child was reaped; if exit or reaping is not confirmed by the deadline, persist cleanup Unknown rather than wait indefinitely or claim the process ended.

setsid, double-fork, closed-pipe, changed-cwd, stale owned-child handle, and controlled identity-loss fixtures never become a claim that unmanaged descendants were cleaned or a reason to signal an unrelated process. Any managed process whose identity or reaping is unconfirmed remains Unknown and cannot pass or produce reusable evidence. A managed-scope pass must explicitly retain the unproved unmanaged-descendant boundary. Actual kernel PID reuse is not claimed as tested in this Work Item.

Cold read and restart retain any Unknown for a WI-managed process and the explicit unmanaged-descendant proof boundary; neither an empty process-group probe nor a later process-cleanup report may promote an unconfirmed managed process to clean or reuse an Unknown attempt.
Full composition supervision still rejects Mac before starting a verifier.
The nine scoped documents state HCI as the sole current North Star: understandable, controllable, explainable, recoverable; the historical map retains its historical identity.

A command's observed exit alone is insufficient for formal verification. Formal success additionally requires confirmed identity-bound reaping of every WI-registered managed process and all existing non-process verification gates. Such success proves only the declared managed-process scope, not arbitrary descendant cleanup.

A WI-local Summary records actual process start, runtime/platform identity, and confirmed direct-child reaping or explicit Unknown without erasing history. The separate final cleanup command reads only that WI, skips reaped entries, and performs bounded cleanup only through a still-held verified owner handle. Missing, stale, ambiguous, or unowned managed entries remain Unknown; neither the command nor a historical PID authorizes a blind signal. Mac may produce a formal managed-scope pass after all registered managed processes are confirmed reaped; an Unknown managed-process attempt never passes or yields reusable evidence. Unmanaged descendant closure remains explicitly unproved, including after a green managed-scope result. Finish, archive, and close retain all other fresh formal evidence and governance gates. Supervisor death never implies handle transfer or cleanup.

Each capable environment must perform fresh formal verification against its own Runtime, Contract, repository identity, and current source snapshot. Mac can qualify for the bounded WI-managed-process scope when all its registered processes are confirmed reaped and no other gate fails. A previous cleanup-Unknown attempt remains historical and is never promoted to clean; Linux and Windows results require separate native evidence and are not inferred from Mac.

The WI-local Summary lifecycle and independent final cleanup command use the same Rust-facing record and result semantics on Linux, macOS, and Windows. Platform-specific ownership and reaping mechanisms remain below that interface and may yield different proof strength; no platform claims cleanup solely from a stored PID, an empty group observation, or another platform's evidence. Normal verification does not require a cross-WI or always-running cleanup service.
previousContract.goal: Use a common Rust execution record and WI-local Summary to register each directly owned process actually started for this Work Item, retain its identity and confirmed reaping or explicit Unknown, and offer a separate bounded final cleanup command for that WI. Formal verification may pass on Mac when every WI-registered, managed process is confirmed reaped and all other verification gates pass. State separately that unmanaged escaped descendants are outside this cleanup proof; never claim complete tree closure. Unconfirmed managed ownership, identity, termination, or reaping remains Unknown and cannot pass or authorize reuse. Do not signal historical numeric PIDs, add a permanent service, or scan other Work Items. Keep full composition supervision unsupported on Mac and HCI the sole North Star in English, Japanese, and Chinese.
